lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Villages, Towns and Cities
lesson.summary: Compare villages, towns and cities in the UK and Pakistan and ask why people settle where they do.
learning_objectives: Explain why places grow where they do

standards.text: Describe and understand key aspects of human geography, including types of settlement and land use; use maps, atlases and aerial images

success_criteria: I can name hamlets, villages, towns and cities
I can give reasons why a settlement grew
I can plan a simple settlement
lesson.real_life: Lahore, Karachi and Islamabad compared with Manchester, Birmingham and a Lake District village, and hill towns such as Murree and Hunza.

warm_up.explanation: A village is a small settlement.

warm_up.prompt: A river can help a settlement grow.
Which is a city in Pakistan?

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: why do people settle where they do?
blocks.say: Today we ask where people live and why. We compare villages, towns and cities.

blocks.alt: An aerial view of a village of red-roofed houses with a white church, winding roads and green fields
blocks.caption: A village seen from above, with a church and surrounding fields.
blocks.credit: Photo by Andreas Gücklhorn on Unsplash
blocks.say: This is a small village seen from above. It has a church, farm fields and winding roads.

blocks.markdown: A **settlement** is a place where people live and work.
blocks.say: A settlement is a place where people live. Settlements come in many sizes.

blocks.markdown: A **hamlet** is the smallest kind of settlement.
blocks.say: A hamlet has just a few homes. A village is bigger, and a town is bigger still.

scenes.caption: Hamlet.
scenes.say: A hamlet has a few houses and little else.

scenes.caption: Village.
scenes.say: A village has homes, a mosque or church, a small shop and a school.

scenes.caption: Town and city.
scenes.say: A town has many shops and schools. A city is larger and has even more services.

question.prompt: Which is the smallest kind of settlement?
question.hint: It has just a few homes.
question.explanation: A hamlet is the smallest settlement.

blocks.alt: An aerial view of a large city skyline with tall skyscrapers beside a river and a suspension bridge
blocks.caption: A large city with tall buildings and bridges beside a river.
blocks.credit: Photo by Patrick Tomasso on Unsplash
blocks.say: Big cities have many people. A megacity has more than ten million people. Karachi and Lahore are megacities.

blocks.markdown: **Services** are things provided to help people.
blocks.say: Services help people, such as hospitals and schools. Facilities are places to use, such as parks and libraries.

scenes.caption: Village.
scenes.say: A village has a small shop and a school.

scenes.caption: Town.
scenes.say: A town adds a market, a bigger school and a clinic.

scenes.caption: City.
scenes.say: A city adds hospitals, universities and big transport links.

question.prompt: A megacity has more than ten million people.
question.explanation: A megacity is a city of over ten million people.

blocks.title: Nabeel's river-bend town
blocks.transcript: Nabeel studies an aerial photo of a town beside a river. The river gives water, food and a way to travel. A bridge at the bend brings roads together. Mohenjo-daro grew in the same way beside the Indus. Manchester grew near rivers and canals that carried goods. Roads, markets and factories made the place bigger. Schools, clinics and parks followed as people moved in. Every settlement has reasons for where it grew.
blocks.caption: Nabeel looks at an aerial photo of a river bend and works out why a town grew there, from Mohenjo-daro to Manchester.

points: A settlement is a place where people live
Hamlet, village, town, city and megacity
blocks.say: Let us remember. Settlements range from hamlets to megacities. Bigger places have more services.

blocks.markdown: The **site** of a settlement is the land it is built on.
blocks.say: People often settle by rivers. Rivers give fresh water, food and a way to travel.

blocks.alt: An old town with stone houses beside a calm river crossed by a stone arch bridge
blocks.caption: A town beside a river with a stone bridge. Rivers and bridges helped towns to grow.
blocks.credit: Photo by Alex Caza on Unsplash
blocks.say: This old town grew beside a river with a stone bridge. The bridge helped trade.

scenes.caption: Manchester.

scenes.caption: Trade.
scenes.say: A bridge or a port can make a settlement a busy trading place.

blocks.markdown: Good transport helps settlements to grow.
blocks.say: Fertile farmland helps villages to feed their people. Roads and railways help towns to grow.

scenes.caption: Farmland.
scenes.say: Flat, fertile land is good for farming. Villages often grow there.

scenes.caption: A junction.

scenes.caption: Growth.
scenes.say: Over time, a village may grow into a town and then a city.
